independently_proved_here: OpenAI lean/docs/197.md detailed scope distinguishes its torsion-bearing characteristic-two and odd-characteristic results from the separate October 4 torsion-free F2 manuscript.

The cited Formanek 1973 Theorem 9 is characteristic zero; Burger-Valette 1998 Lemma 4.1 in characteristic p concludes only tau(e) in {0,1}, while Proposition 4.2 concludes for complex group rings using infinitely many primes.
If ab=1 and ac=0 with c nonzero, then ba is not 1 and e=1-ba is a nontrivial idempotent; its identity trace and augmentation are zero.
source_conditioned_only: The October 4 OpenAI manuscript's finitely presented torsion-free F2 witness.

opportunities.exact_target: For every prime p, field F of characteristic p, torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G, and idempotent e in F[G], prove e=0 or e=1; or give a counterexample.
opportunities.importance: A verified N47/N129 witness would give a torsion-free hyperbolic group whose group ring is not directly finite, hence a nonsofic hyperbolic group by Elek-Szabo. This would settle the existence of nonsofic hyperbolic groups negatively to the universal-soficity question.

primary_prior_work.source: Bartels-Luck-Reich, On the Farrell-Jones Conjecture and its applications, Journal of Topology 1 (2008), p. 63 (preprint p. 9)
primary_prior_work.scope: Explicitly asserts the characteristic-p trivial-idempotent criterion and applies it to torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups. Its separate Theorem 1.12 uses stable finiteness, characteristic zero, or soficity for its K-theoretic direct-finiteness deduction.

primary_prior_work.source: Formanek, Idempotents in Noetherian Group Rings, Canadian Journal of Mathematics 25 (1973), Theorem 9
primary_prior_work.scope: Theorem 9 assumes characteristic zero; Theorem 3 gives a prime-subfield trace statement in arbitrary characteristic.

primary_prior_work.source: Burger-Valette, Idempotents in complex group rings: theorems of Zalesskii and Bass revisited (1998), Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.2
primary_prior_work.scope: Lemma 4.1 gives tau(e) in {0,1} in characteristic p under no p-torsion/no p-power self-conjugacy. Proposition 4.2 gives the complex-group-ring result via infinitely many primes and reduction.

primary_prior_work.source: Elek-Szabo, Sofic groups and direct finiteness, Journal of Algebra 280 (2004)
primary_prior_work.scope: Direct finiteness of sofic-group algebras over arbitrary fields; a verified direct-finiteness failure implies nonsoficity.

opportunities.new_route: Attack the source theorem at its exact modular proof transition, independently of another graph construction. The candidate witness e=1-ba has e^2=e, e nontrivial, tau(e)=0 and augmentation 0, so it is compatible with the cited trace conclusions. A proof must add a support-sensitive or faithful module-dimension invariant that separates a nonzero projective ideal with zero K0 class; alternatively, an acquired witness refutes the printed assertion immediately. Hyperbolic conjugacy/centralizer geometry is a possible input to such a refinement, but no such lemma is known here.
opportunities.load_bearing_missing_lemma: Under torsion-free word-hyperbolic hypotheses, upgrade vanishing of all nonidentity conjugacy-class traces and tau(e) in {0,1} to e=0 or 1, or explicitly demonstrate failure. Trace and rational K0 alone do not do this.
opportunities.early_falsification: If the group presentation and supports are acquired, independently certify torsion-freeness and hyperbolicity, then verify e^2=e and e not in {0,1} in F2[G]. That finite-support witness refutes BLR's stated characteristic-p conclusion. Conversely, reconstruct the exact BLR proof chain and identify any valid step beyond the cited trace conclusion. For a hyperbolic realization, check Delzant's infimum-displacement > 9 delta criterion; if satisfied, the group ring has no zero divisors, contradicting ac=0 with a,c nonzero.
compatibility_obligations: Do not use lean/docs/197.md as a torsion-free input: its detailed characteristic-two scope has odd-prime torsion; its odd-characteristic result also has torsion.
The distinct October 4 OpenAI manuscript states a torsion-free F2 result and a finite two-dimensional classifying complex, not hyperbolicity.
ASTRA N47/N129 hyperbolicity, torsion-free preservation, random graph estimates, disk/Dehn argument, and nonzero witness remain conditional and unmaterialized.
A direct-finiteness failure implies a nontrivial idempotent, but a nontrivial idempotent alone is not equivalent to failure of direct finiteness in a general ring.

opportunities.status: conditional route; exact measurable cohomology unresolved
opportunities.exact_target: Conditional on a countably infinite torsion-free G and F2 witness ab=1, ac=0, c nonzero, decide whether a finite power of K=ker(T_a) is Bernoulli or whether there exist epsilon>0 and an exact pmp G-conjugacy F2^G ~= F2^G x B_epsilon. At epsilon=ln 2 this would give 2^G ~= 4^G.
opportunities.importance: Seward's equal-base-entropy theorem does not decide unequal-base Bernoulli isomorphism. Success would exhibit such an isomorphism for this candidate nonsofic group; failure of the proposed cocycle bridge would not prove nonisomorphism by itself.

primary_prior_work.source: Seward, Bernoulli shifts with bases of equal entropy are isomorphic, Journal of Modern Dynamics 18 (2022), 345-362
primary_prior_work.scope: Equal Shannon entropy bases give isomorphic Bernoulli shifts for all countably infinite groups; no conclusion for unequal base entropy.

primary_prior_work.source: Seward, Positive entropy actions of countable groups factor onto Bernoulli shifts
primary_prior_work.scope: Positive Rokhlin entropy gives Bernoulli factors of at most that entropy; this is a factor theorem, not an isomorphism theorem.

primary_prior_work.source: Adams, Boundary amenability for word hyperbolic groups and an application to smooth dynamics of simple groups, Topology 33 (1994), 765-783
primary_prior_work.scope: Boundary amenability is a possible averaging tool only; it does not imply the exact measurable cocycle identity required here.

opportunities.new_route: Use the reported exact finite-power split K^m ~= X x R to nominate a base pmp isomorphism Q=(j,z):Y ~=_G Y x B_epsilon, then compare the associated extension-cocycle classes in twisted measurable H^1(G action Y,D). This reframes the global conjugacy as one exact class-equality problem, distinct from approximate finite-tail insertion. Algebraic module/extension data may help calculate or obstruct the class; no boundary-amenability-to-H1-vanishing implication is assumed.
opportunities.load_bearing_missing_lemma: For a section s:Y->X and alpha(g,y)=g s(y)-s(gy), find sigma in Aut_G(D), measurable t:Y->D, and Q with alpha(g,jy)-sigma(alpha(g,y))=t(gy)-g t(y) for all g almost everywhere; or prove an obstruction. If the identity holds, the explicit fiber map gives the conjugacy.
opportunities.early_falsification: For a fixed candidate Q and sigma, restrict the cocycle-class difference to an explicit infinite cyclic subgroup <g>. A nonzero class in measurable H1(<g> action Y,D) rules out that exact bridge. A positive result must give measurable t and verify on generators with a proof that the relation extends to all G; approximate convergence and finite word checks do not pass.
